messages.author: Abdelrahman, Noureen
messages.body:
Hello all,
Is there a way I can transform opc water atoms to tip3p? I am trying to use Terachem on a system, and I want to include water molecules in my QM region, but Terachem doesn't work with OPC. So I am wondering if there's a way to transform those specific water molecules that I want to include into TIP3P for Terachem to run?
Thanks,
Noureen

messages.author: He, Amy
messages.body:
Hi!
OPC water has a slightly different geometry than TIP3P water. If you can tolerate the difference or are able to re-optimize water’s geometry in Terachem, you could just replace the atoms’ names and residues’ names in the PDB file (and delete the 4th point in OPC waters).

So I am wondering if there's a way to transform those specific water molecules that I want to include into TIP3P for Terachem to run?
Thanks,
Noureen

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
I think it could be tricky for a few reasons. Opc has 4 points, tip3p has
3. They have different geometries but I don't think the code supports using
both models simultaneously due to parameter name overlap. Also they may
exchange, would maybe you could prevent but is still not trivial. You may
want to consider using opc3 for this application.
